title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government is outlining how it will improve the use and regulation of AI in public services, focusing on safety, transparency and public trust. It highlights new standards, oversight mechanisms, and collaborative efforts with industry and civil society to address the concerns raised in the Committee’s 2020 report.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is outlining how it will regulate the use of artificial intelligence in qualification exams to keep the testing process fair, secure, and trustworthy. The approach, requested by several Secretaries of State, aims to protect learners, uphold exam integrity, and encourage responsible AI practices in the education sector.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyrighted materials are used in building AI systems and assesses the legal, ethical, and practical impacts. It offers recommendations to balance protecting creators’ rights with fostering innovation in AI technology.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government responds to the House of Lords AI committee report, stressing the urgent need for stronger oversight and investment in UK AI development. It outlines new policies and initiatives designed to boost research, tighten regulation, and support ethical AI use while keeping the UK competitive in the global market.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document explains the purpose and responsibilities of a committee that will examine how artificial intelligence should be governed by public standards. It also answers common questions about the committee’s work, its scope, and how it will operate.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission likely outlines CSPL's views and recommendations for how AI should be regulated and overseen.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explains how AI technologies will change the rules and oversight for medical products, focusing on safer, more effective use in healthcare. It outlines steps to follow the AI White Paper principles, such as clear data standards, risk assessments, and accountability, to ensure AI tools meet regulatory and ethical requirements.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organisation the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential defence entity in AI for its size. It focuses on leveraging AI to enhance defence capabilities, improve decision‑making, and uphold high standards of accountability.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport industry to harness AI benefits and address associated risks. It aims to guide the deployment of AI technologies to improve transport services while ensuring safety, privacy, and public confidence.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report examines how copyright‑protected works are being used to train AI systems, assessing compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It outlines current practices, challenges, and recommendations to ensure lawful use of copyrighted materials while fostering AI development.
